source.title: A Few Steps Further: Why Defenses Against Malicious Finetuning Erode Under Continued Training
source.authors: Itay Zloczower; Eyal Lenga; Gilad Gressel; Yisroel Mirsky

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether harmful fine-tuning can erode safety in defended models, using a continued-training cost-curve evaluation rather than the original small-data fine-tuning setup.
record.gate_note: The paper tests continued harmful-only fine-tuning and reports harmfulness outcomes. Its taxonomy and explanations of defenses are arguments about mechanisms, not direct tests of claim versions V3–V7. Results cited from other studies are not recorded as rows. The paper reports dense checkpoint curves in figures; rows below capture the explicit textual outcomes rather than transcribing every plotted checkpoint.
record.test_reason: The study runs harmful-only LoRA fine-tuning (9,000 BeaverTails examples, three epochs, three learning rates) on safety-trained chat models, both undefended and with six anti-fine-tuning defenses. It measures StrongREJECT harmfulness at 21 checkpoints. This bears directly on V1 in a new setting: defended checkpoints and much larger training budgets. It is not one of V1's original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that the fifteen surveyed defenses each encode a finite attacker model that is not enforced after release. In their tests, continued harmful fine-tuning raised harmfulness in all 72 defended runs, and on Llama-3.1 at the highest LR defended models ended within 0.013 of undefended. They conclude that current defenses mostly delay rather than prevent malicious fine-tuning, so fixed-budget resistance should not be treated as durable protection. Exceptions are VAA on Zephyr and cases where harmfulness rose only with capability loss.
record.recipe_differences: Tests continued harmful-only LoRA training of selected defended checkpoints for three epochs, measuring a continuous harmfulness score and capability; it does not reproduce the original small-data fine-tuning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by model, defense, and learning rate; VAA on Zephyr-7B-β stays low in harmfulness at all tested learning rates, while Llama-3.1 defended models at 10−4 finish close to the undefended model.

fits_no_version.finding: In some defended trajectories, harmfulness rises while general capability falls, e.g. CTRAP on Zephyr (0.574→0.501) and VAA on Qwen3 (0.455→0.255).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under continued harmful-only fine-tuning of self-destruction or anchoring defenses, recovered harmfulness can come with capability loss, so harmfulness alone does not establish a capable harmful model.

record.problems: Each trajectory uses a single seed; the three learning rates are separate settings rather than replicates. The attack uses one dataset and objective. The capability proxy has 600 questions and was also used to select some defense configurations. Only six of fifteen defenses were evaluated, none from template T2. The paper notes that its three-epoch attack is finite and cannot establish whether defenses that remain effective within that budget would hold longer.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's checkpoint-by-checkpoint curves for the remaining defended model, defense, and learning-rate combinations are shown in Figures 2–5 but are not transcribed individually; the aggregate conclusion and explicit exceptions or examples are retained. No numerical outcomes from the additional undefended-only trajectories in Figure 6 were included because they do not evaluate defended-model resistance.

untested.parts: The few-to-few-hundred-example regime is not reported numerically; early checkpoints are only plotted and fall inside LR warmup. Refusal rate is not measured; harmfulness is a continuous StrongREJECT usefulness score. Only one attack dataset and objective are used, with a single seed.
No benign fine-tuning attack is tested.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, suffix, or decoding attacks.
The taxonomy argues that defenses encode a finite attacker model. This concerns defense durability, not why standard alignment is shallow, and it is not tested.
No training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens is tested.

missing.what: Undefended safety-trained models attacked with the same recipe. This is the most direct V1 evidence: 12 reference trajectories plus 12 more on Llama-2-13B, Llama-3.2-3B, Mistral-7B, and Qwen2.5-7B. Only Llama-3.1 at LR 1e-4 (0.528) is stated in text; the rest are plotted.

Harmfulness at early checkpoints corresponding to few-to-few-hundred examples (steps ≤48, i.e. ≤384 examples). The text only says it rises within the first epoch over the same token range as undefended. These values are plotted only.
missing.locator: Figures 2–6; Section 5 first paragraph; Appendix F.1

missing.what: Undefended Zephyr and Unlearn-Smooth Zephyr are already more harmful at release than the other defended models, which affects baselines for Zephyr rows.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T3. The question is V1's, but the setting is new: defended checkpoints, a large multi-epoch budget, and a continuous judge score. The record's third V1 label (limits_scope for the 9,000-example budget) was removed. Using more data than the version's regime is an untested part, not a qualification shown by results. Each trajectory uses a single seed and no uncertainty is reported. The capability proxy was also used for defense selection.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the few-to-few-hundred-example regime or directly report refusal rates; the attack trains on 9,000 harmful examples for three epochs, and harmfulness is measured with a continuous judge score.
No benign fine-tuning attack is tested.
No per-token KL divergence or response-position analysis is reported.
No compliant-opening prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change bypass is tested.
No test of whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
The paper discusses defense mechanisms and finite attacker models, but does not test why safety behaviour is shallow in the sense of this version.
No training designed to spread safety across response tokens is tested.

rows.subject: All six defended models on Llama-2-7B-chat, Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and Zephyr-7B-β (72 defended trajectories; aggregate)
rows.size_stated: four backbones: Llama-2-7B-chat, Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Zephyr-7B-β
rows.operation_detail: Continued harmful-only LoRA fine-tuning for three epochs on BeaverTails prompt-response pairs.

conditions.value: StrongREJECT harmfulness score at release versus final checkpoint

rows.measure: Change in mean StrongREJECT harmfulness score from release to final checkpoint
rows.baseline: release checkpoint; aggregate baseline score not stated
rows.value: Mean increase of 0.372; harmfulness increased in all 72 defended trajectories
rows.note: The paper also reports individual increases ranging from 0.022 to 0.520. This is an aggregate across models, defenses, and learning rates.
rows.check: This is an aggregate over 72 defended trajectories. The per-trajectory increases range from 0.022 to 0.520, so some runs barely move. The aggregate hides heterogeneity better shown by R2–R6.

rows.subject: Vaccine on Llama-2-7B-chat
rows.operation_detail: Continued harmful-only LoRA fine-tuning for three epochs.
rows.note: Harmfulness rose substantially but remained below the highest scores reported for some other conditions; the paper does not describe this as near-total removal of refusal.

rows.subject: Six defended models on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Continued harmful-only LoRA fine-tuning for three epochs.
rows.measure: Mean StrongREJECT harmfulness at final checkpoint
rows.baseline: Undefended model under the same attack: 0.528
rows.note: The paper says the defended models finish within 0.013 of the undefended model.

rows.subject: VAA on Zephyr-7B-β
rows.operation_detail: Continued harmful-only LoRA fine-tuning for three epochs.
rows.value: Never exceeds 0.069 at any learning rate
rows.note: This is the stated exception to the general rise in harmfulness; the paper also notes lower capability for this defense.
rows.check: Baseline should read 'release checkpoint (not stated numerically)'. The value is a maximum across all checkpoints and learning rates, not a single endpoint.

rows.subject: CTRAP on Zephyr-7B-β
rows.operation_detail: Continued harmful-only LoRA fine-tuning for three epochs.
rows.note: The paper reports that this recovery coincided with a decline in capability; that capability outcome is recorded separately in R7.

rows.subject: VAA on Qwen3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Continued harmful-only LoRA fine-tuning for three epochs.
rows.note: Harmfulness rises but is non-monotonic and declines from its peak by the final checkpoint.

rows.subject: CTRAP on Zephyr-7B-β

relationships.condition: Harmful-only continued fine-tuning across defended models in general, especially Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct at LR 1e-4 and CTRAP on Zephyr at LR 1e-4
relationships.reason: Harmfulness rose in all 72 defended runs, by 0.372 on average (R1). Llama-3.1 defended models ended at 0.515–0.527 against 0.528 undefended (R3). CTRAP on Zephyr went from 0.028 to 0.521 (R5).
relationships.display_finding: Harmfulness rose in all 72 defended runs, by 0.372 on average. Defended Llama-3.1 models ended at 0.515–0.527 against 0.528 undefended, and CTRAP on Zephyr went from 0.028 to 0.521.

relationships.condition: Vaccine on Llama-2 and VAA on Qwen3 at LR 1e-4
relationships.reason: Erosion was incomplete. Vaccine went from 0.013 to 0.393 (R2). VAA on Qwen3 peaked at 0.363 and ended at 0.241, non-monotonically (R6).
relationships.display_finding: Vaccine harmfulness rose from 0.013 to 0.393, and VAA on Qwen3 peaked at 0.363 before ending at 0.241, so erosion was incomplete and non-monotonic.

relationships.condition: VAA defense on Zephyr-7B-β, all three learning rates, within a 3-epoch budget
relationships.reason: Harmfulness never exceeded 0.069 despite 9,000 harmful examples over three epochs (R4). The authors note a longer attack might still succeed.
relationships.display_finding: Harmfulness never exceeded 0.069 despite 9,000 harmful examples over three epochs, though the authors note a longer attack might still succeed.
